<h3 class="os-card-title">Text-Based ESG Narrative Indicators</h3>

<p class="os-card-desc">
Proposes an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) indicator designed to overcome the limitations of traditional firm-specific ratings, such as inconsistency, infrequency, and bias toward large corporations. The study utilizes a scraped dataset over 390,000 online news articles covering the period from October 2004 to March 2024.
</p>

::: {.os-card-meta}

![Status: Under Construction](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-Under%20Construction-lightgrey.svg)
:::

[Repository Address](https://github.com/Shahram-Dehghan-J/DISES_UNISA_ESG.git){.os-card-link target="_blank"}
:::

::: {.os-card}
<h3 class="os-card-title">Mapping Central Ideas in Textual Corpora</h3>

<p class="os-card-desc">
Introduces a novel, field-agnostic tokenbased dictionary construction framework. The proposed pipeline integrates Part-of-Speech (POS) filtering, Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) weighting, and multi-word ngram extraction to systematically isolate core theoretical constructs without requiring exhaustive domain-specific neural network fine-tuning.
</p>

::: {.os-card-meta} 
![Language: Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Python-blue.svg)  
![Status: Under Construction](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-Under%20Construction-lightgrey.svg)
:::

[Repository Address](https://github.com/Shahram-Dehghan-J/dSEA_UNIPD_Dictionary){.os-card-link target="_blank"}
:::

::: {.os-card}
<h3 class="os-card-title">Internal consistency and stylistic stability of educational textbooks</h3>

<p class="os-card-desc">
Introduces a novel quantitative Textual Consistency Index based on a multi-lingual corpus of 480 historical economics textbooks across English, French, and Italian published between 1890 and 1976t. Utilizing a dual-pipeline natural language processing framework, we systematically quantify micro-structural coherence and pedagogical stability over nearly a century of economic thought.
</p>

::: {.os-card-meta}
